sentences.text:
Petitioners
 Through: Mr. Shashi Shankar & Mr. Sujeet
 Kumar, Advs.
 versus
 State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr

..... Respondents
 Through: Mr. Yudhvir Singh Chauhan, App for
 the State with Si Pradeep, Ps
 Mukherjee Nagar with R-2 in person
 Coram:
 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anish Dayal
 Order
% 20.03.2023 1. Exemption allowed subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

1. This petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.562/2019, under sections 498A/406/34 IPC at PS Mukherjee Nagar on the basis of settlement arrived at between the disputing parties vide MOU dated 9th November, 2021 which is on record of this Court.
2. Petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2-complainant is present in the Court and have been duly identified by the IO and the counsel.
Appearance of petitioner nos. 2 and 3, who are residents of Ludhiana, is exempted on oral prayer by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
3. Petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 were married on 3rd September. 2016 and one female child was born out of wedlock.
Pursuant to the differences between themselves have now obtained the decree of divorce by mutual consent dated 3rd August, 2022.
4. As per the settlement, in terms of para 3 thereof, certain articles are to be returned to the respondent no.2 by petitioner no.1 from matrimonial home at Ludhiana.

It is accordingly directed that quashing of the present FIR shall be subject to return of articles, which may be collected by the respondent no.2, either personally or through her authorised person, at her own cost and expense,
within next 2 weeks and on an advance communication to petitioner no.1 in this regard.

Respondent no.2 accordingly confirms that she will accordingly organize these articles to be collected and the petitioner no.1 undertakes to provide all necessary cooperation and assistance in this behalf for Abhey Dua @ Abhey Dua And Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160605504/
1 return of the articles as per the settlement.

entities.text: Abhey Dua @ Abhey Dua And Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.

Consequently, the of FIR No.562/2019, under sections 498A/406/34 IPC at PS Mukherjee Nagar and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed subject to compliance of all the aspects and conditions of the settlement between the parties and undertaking by the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 in the Court today.
It is however made clear that the said settlement will not affect the rights of the minor child in future.
6. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
7. Petition is disposed of accordingly.
Pending applications (if any) are disposed of as infructuous.
8. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.

ANISH DAYAL, J MARCH 20, 2023/sm Abhey Dua @ Abhey Dua And Anr vs State Of Nct Of Delhi And Anr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160605504/
